title: streetCryptid — device health (is each phone alive?)
description: The absence dashboard. Every other view explains a ping that happened; this one is about phones that have stopped producing pings at all. The top row carries the checks that would otherwise be alert rules — surfaced here rather than sent anywhere. Built on span-derived Prometheus metrics (90d) rather than traces (7d), because the question is usually "when did this last work?" and by the time anyone asks, the traces are gone.

panels.title: Conditions worth noticing — deliberately not alerts
panels.description: These are the checks that would otherwise page someone. They are counts, on a page, on purpose: nothing here sends a notification. Zero across the row means every phone that has reported recently is behaving.

panels.title: Phones not waking (6h)
panels.description: Devices that have had no bg.wake for six hours. This is the core background failure: the OS has stopped delivering location and nothing else on the device will say so. Six hours is chosen against the platform floor — the periodic refresh is ~15 min at best and both OSes defer it much further under battery pressure, so a shorter window would be noise. Confirm in the state table below: sharing.enabled=true with task.location_running=false is the bug.

panels.title: Phones not reporting state (2h)
panels.description: Devices that have emitted no device.health for two hours. Either the periodic task itself has stopped, or the device cannot reach the collector — and those two are told apart by what arrives NEXT. The app ships from a durable journal, so a phone that was merely offline delivers its backlog later with the ORIGINAL timestamps and a large telemetry.queued, and the gap fills in retrospectively. A gap that stays empty is a phone that genuinely stopped.

panels.title: Runtime wedged / storage gone (1h)
panels.description: bg.session.stranded, bg.session.watchdog, bg.teardown.timeout or storage.degraded in the last hour. These are terminal and none of them are self-healing. A hung native teardown once wedged every later session and cost an iPhone 19 hours of silence; storage.degraded means persistence fell back to memory, so the outbox, friend pool and sharing intent are lost on every process death. Any non-zero value here deserves a look.

panels.title: Publishing but not pushing (1h)
panels.description: Devices sealing and publishing envelopes without pushing them to the stash, so the fixes exist only in the local replica. Friends online at that exact moment still see them live; everyone else never will — the precise gap the stash exists to close, and completely invisible from the sending side. Check trail.push.app for native.push.failed, and whether the device has any durable peer tickets at all.

targets.expr: count((sum by (device_id) (increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="streetcryptid-app", span_name="publish.fix"}[1h])) > 5) and (sum by (device_id) (increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="streetcryptid-app", span_name="trail.push.app"}[1h])) < 1)) or vector(0)

panels.title: Last seen — minutes since each device last emitted ANY span
panels.description: The first panel to read. A device whose value keeps climbing has stopped talking to the collector entirely: either it is not being woken, or it cannot reach us. `device.health` records tell the two apart — see the state table below, whose `telemetry.queued` grows in the second case and does not exist in the first.

panels.title: Background wakes — bg.wake /min by device
panels.description: Flat zero on a device whose last `device.health` said sharing.enabled=true is the core failure this whole dashboard exists for: the OS has stopped delivering location to us and nothing else will say so. Empty and errored wakes are included on purpose — being woken and handed nothing is a different fault from not being woken, and both are wakes.

panels.title: The pipeline, per device — wake → fix → publish → push
Publishes — publish.fix /min by device
panels.description: A device waking but not publishing has passed the OS gate and failed one of ours: read `Drops by reason` below, then the `engine.ingest` spans in Tempo.

panels.title: Pushes — trail.push.app /min by device
panels.description: Publishing without pushing means envelopes are being written to the LOCAL replica and never leaving the phone — a friend who was not online at that exact moment never sees them, which is the whole reason the stash exists. Compare against the publish rate beside it.

panels.title: Health records — device.health /min by device
panels.description: The liveness assertion itself, emitted once per periodic refresh and on foreground resume. A gap here with no gap in bg.wake means the periodic task (BGTaskScheduler / WorkManager) has stopped, not location.

panels.title: Why — drops, terminal states, and the last known device state
Drops by reason /min
panels.description: Every sc.drop_reason across the pipeline. Some are benign and expected (sampling-suspended, coalesced, fgs-start-blocked on a refresh trigger); the ones worth chasing are storage-*, outbox-*, cadence-rearm-failed and engine-*-failed, which are all silent on the device itself.

panels.title: Terminal native-runtime states /h — these should always be zero
panels.description: bg.session.stranded, bg.session.watchdog, bg.teardown.timeout and storage.degraded. Each one means the process-wide native chain hung or the device is running with no durable storage — the 2026-08-18 class of failure, where a single wedged teardown cost an iPhone 19 hours of silence. Any non-zero value here deserves a look, not a threshold.

panels.title: Last known device state — permissions, OS tasks, and ages (newest device.health per device)
panels.description: What the OS actually thinks, as of each device's most recent health record. Read it for MISMATCHES rather than for any single value: sharing.enabled=true with task.location_running=false is the bug; perm.background=denied or perm.accuracy=reduced explains a phone that wakes but never produces a usable fix; storage.backend=memory means nothing that device persists survives a restart; a large telemetry.queued means the data is fine and our collector is what it cannot reach.

targets.query: { name = "device.health" } | select(resource.device.id, resource.service.version, span.trigger, span.sharing.enabled, span.sharing.recipients, span.task.location_running, span.task.refresh_registered, span.task.fence_registered, span.task.refresh_status, span.perm.background, span.perm.ios_scope, span.perm.accuracy, span.storage.backend, span.outbox.pending, span.telemetry.queued, span.last_wake_age_ms, span.last_fix_age_ms, span.last_publish_age_ms, span.last_push_age_ms, span.battery.low_power, span.net.connected)
